module_title: The Himalayas and Northern Mountains - Basic Understanding
introduction: The Himalayas are the highest and youngest fold mountains in the world. They form a massive arc along the northern border of India, stretching for about 2,400 km from the Indus River gorge in the west to the Brahmaputra River gorge in the east.

core_concepts.title: The Great Himalayas (Himadri)
core_concepts.description: The northernmost, highest, and most continuous range. The average height is 6,000 meters. It contains the world's highest peaks, including Mt. Everest (in Nepal) and Kangchenjunga (in India).

core_concepts.title: The Lesser Himalayas (Himachal)
core_concepts.description: Lies to the south of the Himadri. Its average height is between 3,700 and 4,500 meters. The Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar, and Mahabharat ranges belong here. All famous hill stations (Shimla, Nainital, Darjeeling) are located in this range.

core_concepts.title: The Outer Himalayas (Shiwaliks)
core_concepts.description: The southernmost and lowest range (900-1100 meters) of the Himalayas. It is made up of unconsolidated sediments (gravel and alluvium) brought down by rivers from the main Himalayan ranges.

core_concepts.title: Highest Peaks
core_concepts.description: Mt. Everest (8,848.86 m) in Nepal is the world's highest. K2 / Godwin Austin (8,611 m) is India's highest peak, but it lies in the Karakoram range (PoK). Kangchenjunga (8,598 m) in Sikkim is the highest peak of the Himalayas in India.

important_entities.name: Duns (or Doons)
important_entities.significance: The longitudinal valleys lying between the Lesser Himalayas and the Shiwaliks are called Duns in the west. Examples: Dehradun, Kotli Dun, Patli Dun.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If an exam asks 'Highest Peak of India', the answer is K2. If it asks 'Highest Peak of the Himalayas in India', the answer is Kangchenjunga. K2 is part of the Trans-Himalayas, not the true Himalayas.

exam_strategy_tips: Always remember that the Himalayas are 'Young Fold Mountains' while the Aravallis are 'Old Fold Mountains'.
Hill stations belong exclusively to the Lesser Himalayas (Himachal). This is a highly repeated MCQ.
